newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SOCCER-VALENCIA TAKE LEGAL ACTION AGAINST FIFA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VALENCIA TAKE LEGAL ACTION AGAINST FIFA.

text.p: Spanish soccer club Valencia and their Croatian striker Goran Vlaovic have lodged a complaint with the European Commission over a transfer fee claimed by Italian club Padova, it was announced on Tuesday.

The lawyer for Valencia and Vlaovic, Jean-Louis Dupont, who also represents Belgian Jean-Marc Bosman, said in a statement that FIFA had ordered Valencia to pay Padova $3.8 million for Vlaovic even though his contract had expired.
Dupont said FIFA's rule that allowed transfer fees for non-EU players at the end of their contracts violated article 85 of the Rome Treaty banning competition restrictions within the EU.
He added that the Bosman ruling did not apply only to EU players.

Bosman threw European soccer into turmoil in 1995 when his legal fight over a blocked transfer culminated in a Court of Justice ruling that UEFA's transfer fee rules and restrictions on the number of foreign players in teams infringed EU law.
Vlaovic moved to Valencia last July but Padova, who had been relegated from Italy's serie A two months earlier, later claimed "compensation for training".
